findings.statement: a segment opened after the store has changed mode is in the store's mode, not the option's
findings.detail: after a scan the store reports MADV_RANDOM false and the kernel reports VM_RAND_READ on 0 of 2 segment mappings; after a seal took it from 2 to 6 segments, 0 of 6. Read from /proc/self/smaps rather than from the store's own record, because the failure this catches is the two disagreeing -- a segment opened with the option's mode instead of the store's leaves every read correct and only the advice stale

findings.statement: over a store with several segments the adaptive advice beats both fixed settings on a phased workload
findings.detail: adaptive 40575 ops/s against the kernel's default 6572 (adaptive vs default: greater 6.174x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 4.8%/4.2%)) and fixed MADV_RANDOM 20365 (adaptive vs random: greater 1.992x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 4.8%/1.4%)), over 2 cycles of 20 point reads and 8 scans of 100 on a store of 65.1 MB in several segments against a 32 MB cap

findings.statement: on a workload with no phases the adaptive advice is not resolvably slower than the better fixed setting
findings.detail: alternating one point read and one scan of 100, 20 of each: default 11392 ops/s, random 17768, adaptive 41107. Against the better fixed setting (random), adaptive vs random: greater 2.313x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 5.5%/21.8%)

findings.statement: on a store that fits in memory the adaptive advice costs nothing against the kernel's default
findings.detail: a warm 8 MB store inside the 32 MB cap: adaptive 10528 ops/s against the kernel's default 7498, 140.4% of it (adaptive vs default: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.404, p=0.2101) -- within noise, not a result). This is the case f66 could not ask, because every one of its arms ran against a file eight times its page cache. Here the advice can win nothing and can only cost -- a madvise per segment per phase change, and a branch per operation -- so a resolvable loss makes Adaptive a bad default however well it does out-of-core

notes: f66 measured this policy over a single Blob and a single mapping. A Db maps one file per segment, so a transition is one madvise per live segment rather than one, and the memtable is not advised at all -- this is the same policy priced where it actually ships
